subject: TideGate integration: SDK/auth/routing policy checklist and next steps
messages:
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Samara Jones <samara@tidegate.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-11T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: TideGate integration: SDK/auth/routing policy checklist and next steps

Hi Samara — thanks again for the time today. Short recap + concrete next steps from our side so TideGate can spin up a sandbox integration with minimal friction.

Call summary (30m):
- Product fit: primary use is customer chat (low-latency session routing) + nightly batch embedding jobs for search indexing.
- Security: TideGate prefers OIDC service accounts + short-lived client creds; also open to an API-key fallback for CI workflows.
- Regions: us-west-2 primary, eu-west-1 for EU customers (multi-region requirement).
- Migrations: plan to progressively route 10% canary -> 50% -> full after smoke tests.

What Redwood will provide (deliverables):
1) Integration runbook draft (Drive link attached). Contains SDK quickstart, sample policy JSON, and example routing CSV.
2) Proposed model-routing table (attached) mapping workload -> model family, latency SLO, cost tier, and fallback chain.
3) SDK snippet for auth (OIDC + API-key patterns) and an example structured output template for tool-calling / order extraction.
4) Short recording of today's demo attached.

Immediate asks for TideGate:
- Confirm sandbox VPC + whether we should use VPC peering or PrivateLink for Dedicated (if on-prem, flag now).
- Provide a service account OIDC issuer url and a test client id (we will not use prod credentials).
- Confirm that eu-west-1 should be enabled on day 1 or delayed to canary phase.

Next steps / timeline:
- EOD Wed: Redwood to share runbook v1 + routing CSV (attached).
- Thu: TideGate to provision sandbox + share OIDC test creds.
- Following week: Redwood will deploy routing policy to staging and run latency/cost smoke tests.

Attachments: 20280411-call-recording.mp4, tidegate-integration-runbook-v1.docx, proposed-routing-table.csv

High-level recommended routing policy (preview):
- Chat (session): latency-first -> primary model: redwood-gptx-8-lr (low-latency), fallback: redwood-gptx-8-quant, final fallback: redwood-gptx-7 (cost-saver).
- Embeddings (batch nightly): cost-first -> primary model: embed-512-v3-quant, fallback: embed-384-v2.
- Reranker (search recency): cross-encoder-rr-v2 for rerank step, with deterministic seeding for A/B reproducibility.

I put Neha and Monica on-copy to coordinate the SDK/auth snippets and the policy JSON. Rishi will help scope SLA/latency targets for the canary.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30m follow-up if you want to walk through the runbook line-by-line.

—
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
From: Samara Jones <samara@tidegate.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Cc: TideGate Platform <platform@tidegate.ai>
Date: 2028-04-11T18:25:00-07:00
Subject: Re: TideGate integration: SDK/auth/routing policy checklist and next steps

Aditya — great recap, really helpful. A few clarifications from our infra team after the call: 

1) Regions: we'll enable us-west-2 in sandbox immediately. eu-west-1 will be enabled during canary (target: +2 weeks) — this is fine with your proposed rollout.
2) Auth: OIDC service account is preferred for production. We'll provision a test OIDC issuer and a short-lived client for you by Thu. For CI pipelines we will accept API key -> rotate via our vault; we would like your SDK to document both flows.
3) Routing behavior: for chat we want a latency ceiling of 180ms p95 for the primary route. If p95 breaches for 3m, we want automatic fallback to the quantized variant. For embeddings batch jobs, cost is the primary criteria — pick the quantized embed model by default and only fall back to higher-fidelity if similarity degradation > 1.5% on our eval set.
4) Reranker: we plan to run dense retrieval (embed index) + cross-encoder reranker for top 50 results. Can you include an example pipeline in the runbook and the recommended tokenization/rep scoring seed?

Couple of asks: please include an SDK quickstart snippet for Node/Python showing OIDC token exchange and a sample structured-output schema for the tool call we demoed (order-confirmation extraction). Also, can you confirm whether Redwood supports pinned model versions per-route (we need pinned for canary rollback)?

We'll provision the sandbox VPC and let you know when the OIDC test creds are ready. Thanks again, this is moving quickly on our side.

Best,
Samara Jones
Director, Platform Engineering
TideGate

Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-12T08:05:00-07:00
Subject: internal: TideGate routing policy draft + action checklist (do not forward)

Team — internal follow-up after Samara's reply. Putting a concrete checklist and the first draft of the routing policy here. Please keep internal until we finalize v1.

Action items (short):
- Neha: produce Node + Python SDK quickstart showing OIDC token exchange, and a fallback example for API-key rotation. Include code comment showing how to pin model versions per-route. ETA: Thu EOD.
- Monica: update the runbook with explicit routing JSON for our staging policies and include the smoke-test script (latency/proc-cost harness). ETA: Fri noon.
- Rishi: define the latency SLO gating logic for auto-fallback (p95 threshold and cool-down windows). Also propose SLA language for canary. ETA: Fri EOD.

Routing policy draft (plain English):
- Workload: chat-session (interactive)
  - Primary: redwood-gptx-8-lowlatency (SLO: p95 <= 180ms)
  - Fallback-1: redwood-gptx-8-quant (trigger: p95 > 180ms for 3 consecutive minutes)
  - Fallback-2: redwood-gptx-7-cost (slow, cost-saver)
  - Region routing: prefer us-west-2, fallback to eu-west-1 only for EU-origin sessions.

- Workload: embeddings (batch nightly)
  - Primary: embed-512-v3-quant (cost-first, expected tokens/day budget)
  - Fallback: embed-384-v2 (if eval recall drop > 1.5%)

- Workload: reranker (top-k cross-encoder)
  - Primary: rr-cross-enc-v2 (pinned), deterministic seed for reproducible scores, retract if drift > 2% on validation set.

Notes on implementation details to include in runbook:
- SDK: show example of adding a route header (x-redwood-route) and pinning field (model_version) in the request payload.
- Auth: OIDC flow sample + short-lived token refresh loop; fallback to API key if token endpoint unreachable for >2m.
- Structured output: include JSON schema example for tool-calling (order_id, items[], total_amount, confirmed:boolean).
- Batching/caching: recommend prefix KV cache for session context to cut token spend; include conservative TTLs for embeddings cache (24h).

I'll merge Neha's SDK snippets into the runbook and send v1 to Samara once we have the OIDC test creds.

—
Aditya

Subject: Re: TideGate integration: SDK/auth/routing policy checklist and next steps

Aditya / team — thanks, that all looks good. We started provisioning the sandbox VPC this morning and will share the OIDC test issuer + client id by Thu morning. A couple quick confirmations:

- Pinned model versions per-route: yes, we need that for canary. Your note about model_version in the request payload is sufficient — we'll test pinning during canary.
- EU region: we will not enable eu-west-1 in sandbox immediately. Please plan the canary to run only in us-west-2; we'll flip eu-west-1 in the canary +2 week window.
- Reranker pipeline: we'll provide a 1k-sample eval set for the embedding + rerank test. If you can include the deterministic-seed example and a small scoring harness that would be perfect.

We'll review the runbook when you share v1. Appreciate the clear checklist and the proposed fallback rules — will circle back if our security team asks for any additional constraints on token lifetimes.

Best,
Samara
